title: Missing proof asset before finishing
facts: The approved brief requires three proof moments. Two source clips are present; the third asset ID points to an unreadable file. The user asks to start final color and export now.

title: Cut-rate vanity versus comprehension
facts: A 16-second product video is understandable at 11 cuts. The user demands 30 cuts because fast edits always retain attention; at that pace the price and proof are unreadable.

title: Unmotivated continuity break
facts: Two attractive shots reverse screen direction and make the product appear to move backward. The disorientation has no approved purpose.

title: Misleading concealment of condition
facts: A used product has a visible repaired area. The user asks for a crop and heavy grade that hides it while the copy implies current condition is shown.

title: Missing CTA coverage
facts: The approved CTA block has no usable footage. Unrelated stock footage could fill the duration but would imply a different product.

title: Washed-out export before blind saturation
facts: Phone clips look normal in one viewer and washed out after export. Input transfer metadata and output tags have not been checked. The user asks to add saturation.

title: Noise reduction damages dialogue
facts: Dialogue contains mild room noise. Aggressive denoise removes consonants and pumps between words; the original remains understandable.

title: Incorrect automatic captions
facts: Automatic captions change a model name and price. Timing also covers the visual proof. Audio is clear.

title: Uncontrolled variant drift
facts: Variant B tests only hook text, but it also has brighter grade, faster cuts and clearer proof than A.

title: Remembered delivery preset conflicts with live evidence
facts: A remembered social-platform preset conflicts with the current official upload page and the source frame rate. No test upload exists.

title: Successful export log without artifact inspection
facts: The NLE export reports success. The produced file has not been decoded or watched; a prior export from this project lost its audio track.

title: Justified continuity-rule violation
facts: A deliberate jump cut creates urgency and remains understandable. The brief permits stylistic discontinuity and a blind comparison favors it. Source identity, claims and delivery checks are valid.
